name: MemServe: Context Caching for Disaggregated LLM Serving with Elastic Memory Pool
problem: Serving has moved from stateless to STATEFUL - context caching and disaggregated inference both extend the lifetime and reach of the KV cache - which creates an architectural problem no single existing mechanism solved: the KV cache now has to be managed as a shared, elastic resource across instances rather than as per-instance scratch.
mechanism: Claims to combine CONTEXT CACHING with DISAGGREGATED INFERENCE for the first time in one system, unified by MemPool: an ELASTIC MEMORY POOL that manages distributed memory and the KV caches across serving instances behind a small set of APIs, so the same pool serves both roles instead of the two mechanisms each managing their own memory. A global scheduler sits on top and raises reuse with a GLOBAL PROMPT TREE locality-aware policy - a tree over prompts rather than per-instance exact-prefix matching, which is the same insight SGLang's RadixAttention brings to a single engine, here applied across the disaggregated fleet. The framing that matters for a deployment reader: disaggregation used to be a way to stop cache locality, and MemServe's claim is that you can have both if the memory tier itself is elastic.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim is qualitative and stated as such: 'significantly improves job completion time and time-to-first-time' [time-to-first-token]. No ratio, baseline, or hardware configuration is given in the abstract, so speedup_reported records the claim and the ABSENCE of a number rather than reconstructing one - the same treatment given to InfiniGen in the repo.
